subject: Ability registry
notes: Every line of effect text is transcribed verbatim from the in-game Active Abilities panel.
`cooldown` and `active_time` come from the in-game panel; neither published source carries them.
`note` holds the italic line the game prints under the effect - either that the ability works passively once equipped, or that it does not take up a common slot in the Active Abilities panel.
`no_common_slot` marks an ability that does not consume one of the tree's ability slots.
Activation charge and health costs to use an ability come from the in-game Cost line, cross-checked against the Fextralife ability table.
The source labels the fourth row of four-level abilities 'Lv. 3'; levels here are numbered by position.
Abilities have no prerequisites in either source - they are learned independently of the perk graph.
Gates: manual, corruption <n>, road shrine, vrakhir blood (a Phial of Vrakhir Blood), or none.
Some levels cost skill points but no time segments, so `time_segments` can be 0.
A level whose cost the game hides is one the capture's save had already bought; those costs are kept from the published tables.

`kind` is active or passive, decided by use_cost: anything that pays an activation charge or health is active. Passive abilities still take an ability slot - they work once equipped in the Active Ability panel.
`story_granted` marks an ability whose first level the story hands you: it costs no skill points and no time segments to learn. Upgrades past level 1 are paid for normally.

`text_source` records where each level row's text came from: `game` (read from the in-game panel), `game8` (still the Game8 table, never re-read from the game), or `placeholder` (a padlocked story node that prints no effect line).

`units` is a level row's damage in units of character power, which does not change with character level; `effect_template` is the row with each figure replaced by a slot. Multiply and truncate to get the figure at any level. See `scaling`.

`over_time` marks a row whose figure repeats: `count` times `per` second or hit. Its total is that figure multiplied by `count`, which is what makes it comparable with an ability that deals its damage at once.

scaling.note: A displayed damage figure is floor(units x power). `units` belongs to the ability level and never changes; `power` belongs to the character and is measured here at levels 9, 15 and 20. To restate a row at level L, interpolate power between the two nearest anchors and truncate - the game truncates rather than rounds. A row's `scale_tree`, when present, names the stat it follows instead of the tree it sits in.
scaling.closed_form_note: Swordmastery's power is exactly 11*(level+2)/4 at all three measured levels, so Dirty Trick level 1 is 11*(level+2) on the nose. The other two trees are not linear in character level and three anchors cannot settle their shape, so they are interpolated rather than given a formula.
scaling.witchcraft_caveat: Witchcraft's power is not a function of character level alone. Two captures at level 20 differ by about 11%, so a perk or world-progress multiplier is folded into these figures - Astral Communion and Witchcraft Mastery both add percentage damage. Witchcraft numbers are therefore indicative rather than exact for a given character.
scaling.observations_note: Every figure read from a panel, by character level. verify_perks.py restates each row at each level through the model and fails if it does not come back to what the panel showed.
